data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when failure is the installation condition rather than the outcome: the shown-to-fail-first ritual makes the test's authority depend on the subject failing before the test is trusted. The 1-of-9 compile.py mutation was lost because the mutation did not cause a failure during installation, so the test never activated for that path. The 4/4 to 6/7 modules constrained their mutations because their mutations did cause installation-time failures, which triggered the guard. The 3-of-26 result measures how many mutations fail loudly enough during installation to be caught by a fail-first test.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the lost compile.py mutation would fail loudly during installation but was still missed, then installation visibility is not the mechanism.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4 modules caught runtime-only mutations, then the fail-first threshold does not explain their success.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the ritual was run identically for all modules, then differential installation visibility cannot explain the distribution.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1-of-9 loss is shown to be a reporting error rather than a silent pass, the claim is confounded.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Shown-to-fail-first installation creates a threshold effect: only failures that manifest during the installation ritual are recorded as constraints. Failures that would manifest later, or only under different inputs, are described rather than constrained because the test never runs in the mode that would expose them. The distribution reflects the proportion of mutations that are installation-visible versus runtime-visible in each module.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
